source.title: Preventing Premature Commitment in Coding Agents with an Evidence-Conditioned Execution Layer

assessments.primary_source_quality: Very strong for a recent preprint: all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, two language models, two agent scaffolds, no model retraining/scaffold modification, structured-vs-natural-language comparison, operation-level ablations, and efficiency measurement. No independent external replication was identified.
assessments.quantitative_result: ECLoop raises Pass@1 by +4.8 to +11.8 percentage points across the tested model/scaffold conditions and lowers average token consumption by up to 12.1%. Each of its three operations contributes distinct value, and structured evidence conditions outperform an equivalent natural-language summary.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong. The execution layer is evaluated against the same coding-agent scaffolds without the layer, and the structured-condition representation is explicitly compared against a natural-language-summary condition. Multi-model/multi-scaffold testing supplies useful robustness.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for evidence-conditioned postponement/redirection preventing premature coding commitment in SWE-bench Verified. The candidate O proposal narrows the mechanism to specific high-consequence action classes, which is faithful but not itself directly tested outside coding actions.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: The source gives a concrete execution-layer mechanism and standard benchmark setting. This comparator did not independently run the code and no official repository was established in this pass.
assessments.external_replication: No independent replication located; cross-model/scaffold and component ablations provide substantial within-study robustness.
assessments.failure_evidence: Directly supports the premise that merely placing evidence/reminders in context is weaker than mechanically conditioning selected actions on evidence actually observed.
scope_limits: Coding repository actions on SWE-bench Verified, not arbitrary O decisions.
The quality of compiled evidence conditions matters; speculative/overbroad conditions could create rigid blocking.
The result validates structured execution gating for mechanically checkable evidence, not universal procedural gates for semantic judgments.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for ECLoop's evidence-conditioned execution in the tested coding-agent setting.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: B-/B until O compares enforce-vs-remind-vs-no-gate on narrowly selected O actions with latency, false-block and downstream-success controls.

source.title: Accurate Failure Prediction in Agents Does Not Imply Effective Failure Prevention

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary intervention study: it explicitly separates offline critic prediction quality from causal deployment effect, measures end-to-end task outcomes across regimes, and validates a 50-task predeployment sign-of-effect pilot. No independent replication identified.
assessments.quantitative_result: A binary LLM critic with AUROC 0.94 causes a 26-percentage-point performance collapse on one model while having near-zero effect on another. Across tested benchmarks, intervention ranges from 0 to -26 pp on high-success regimes but improves the high-failure ALFWorld regime by +2.8 pp (p=0.014). A 50-task predeployment pilot correctly anticipates whether the intervention is likely to help or harm in the reported evaluations.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong because task success is measured directly with versus without intervention rather than using critic AUROC as a surrogate. The pilot is small and its calibration/generalization across unseen task families needs broader validation.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for the core rule that monitors must be evaluated as complete interventions and that a small end-to-end pilot can detect harmful deployment in the tested settings. It does not prove 50 tasks is universally sufficient or establish one optimal intervention policy.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: The primary source specifies the critic/intervention comparison and benchmark outcomes; independent execution not performed here.
assessments.failure_evidence: Exceptionally strong for the failure premise: high predictive AUROC can coexist with severe causal harm when interventions disrupt trajectories that would have recovered/succeeded.
scope_limits: Pilot size and task distribution are paper-specific.
A monitor that helps in a high-failure regime can hurt a high-success regime; no universal intervention threshold follows.
Effect depends on both critic errors and recovery/disruption behavior of the base agent.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for the causal failure claim and B+/A- for a small predeployment pilot as a sign check in the reported tasks.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: B- until an O-specific pilot shows predictive value for O monitor/intervention configurations.

source.title: Accurate Failure Prediction in Agents Does Not Imply Effective Failure Prevention

assessments.primary_source_quality: Same strong primary intervention study as above.
assessments.quantitative_result: The observed sign reversal across base success regimes directly demonstrates a disruption-recovery tradeoff: intervention can recover some failing trajectories while destroying would-be successes. The +2.8 pp ALFWorld gain and up-to -26 pp degradation elsewhere show base failure/recoverability changes net value.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for existence of the tradeoff, but the worker's exact expected-value threshold formula is not directly implemented/evaluated as a policy in the source.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for conditioning intervention decisions on estimated recoverability/base failure regime; weaker for any specific threshold estimator or cost equation.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Not independently rerun in this pass.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence against thresholding solely on critic confidence or AUROC.
scope_limits: Recoverability is counterfactual and may be hard to estimate online.
No exact universal decision threshold is established.
Costs of delay, false alarms and partial recovery vary by environment.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for the disruption-recovery tradeoff as a causal observation.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- for an explicit recoverability-aware threshold until directly calibrated on O held-out intervention outcomes.

source.title: AgentForesight: Online Auditing for Early Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems

assessments.primary_source_quality: Useful primary source with AFTraj-2K across Coding, Math and Agentic domains, an external Who&When evaluation, a compact 7B auditor and step-localization metrics. Unsafe-step labels rely partly on multi-LLM consensus, introducing possible judge bias, and no intervention policy outcome is established by the abstract.
assessments.quantitative_result: AgentForesight-7B is reported to outperform leading proprietary models including GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro by up to +19.9% on its auditing metrics with roughly 3x lower step-localization error. It predicts continue versus alarm from the current prefix and targets the earliest decisive error boundary.
assessments.matched_baseline: Good for predictor/localizer comparison; weak for the proposed O historical failure-boundary dataset and for any downstream intervention benefit.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for the feasibility/value of prefix-only early-boundary prediction. Low for the O proposal to label future-success-collapse boundaries and train a cheap predictor, because label reliability and intervention efficacy remain unresolved.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Project page is public; this comparator did not inspect/run full released training artifacts.
assessments.failure_evidence: Supports moving from post-hoc full-trajectory blame to online prefix-localization, but not that alarms should automatically interrupt execution.
scope_limits: Training labels can inherit multi-LLM judge error/correlation.
Auditing metric gains are not task-success intervention gains.
Earliest decisive boundary is itself an uncertain counterfactual construct.
O-specific historical traces may differ markedly from AFTraj-2K.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for the reported online failure-boundary prediction/localization system.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C for building/training on O boundary labels until label validity and downstream benefit are measured.

source.title: PIVOT: Bridging Planning and Execution in LLM Agents via Trajectory Refinement

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary system paper across DeepPlanning and GAIA with an explicit PLAN-INSPECT-EVOLVE-VERIFY loop, monotonic acceptance, autonomous and HITL variants, constraint-satisfaction outcomes and token efficiency. Strongest exact gain in the abstract is HITL and the autonomous component is less quantitatively specified there.
assessments.quantitative_result: The source reports up to 94% relative improvement in constraint satisfaction with HITL feedback, substantial gains for a fully autonomous variant, and up to 3x-5x fewer tokens than competing refinement methods.
assessments.matched_baseline: Useful system comparisons to competing refinement methods, but the worker's specific rule 'replace only if a named discrepancy is fixed and a precommitted score improves' is a distilled O adaptation rather than a directly isolated single-component ablation.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for feedback-driven executable trajectory refinement with monotonic acceptance. Weaker for attributing gains to monotonic acceptance alone or for transfer to O planning.
assessments.failure_evidence: Supports the premise that coherent plans can fail execution constraints and that free-form replanning can be replaced by measured plan-execution discrepancy optimization.
scope_limits: Strongest headline improvement uses human-in-the-loop feedback.
System-level result bundles planning, inspection, textual gradients, evolution, global verification and monotonic acceptance.
A monotonic score can optimize the wrong metric if the precommitted evaluator is invalid.
Exact autonomous effect sizes need deeper full-text extraction before upgrading the grade.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for PIVOT's system-level refinement mechanism, B- for monotonic acceptance as the isolated causal component.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- until O tests matched free-form-replan versus discrepancy-conditioned monotonic replacement under a valid held-out score.

cross_source_synthesis: ECLoop is one of the strongest direct intervention mechanisms assessed so far because it improves task success across the full SWE-bench Verified set and shows structured enforcement beats equivalent natural-language reminders.

The failure-prediction study supplies direct causal evidence that evaluator quality metrics are not sufficient: intervention policy must be measured end-to-end, and the sign of effect can reverse with base-agent recoverability.
AgentForesight is credible as a boundary-prediction measurement system but should not be upgraded into an intervention mechanism without causal deployment results.
PIVOT supports measured monotonic plan refinement, but the exact O rule is only one abstraction of a bundled system-level result and depends critically on evaluator validity.
